headline_hook: Karpathy Warns LLMs Argue Too Well While Meta Ships SAM 3.1 and LeCun Cracks World Models

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Karpathy's 4-hour experiment reveals the core danger of LLM-assisted thinking: these models don't seek truth, they seek coherence — and the better they get at writing, the harder it becomes for humans to distinguish a well-argued position from a correct one. This isn't a safety hypothetical; it's a workflow problem hitting every builder who uses AI for decision-making today.

model_literacy.relevance: LeCun's team claims a formal guarantee against representation collapse — the failure mode where a model's internal representations converge to a single point, losing all useful information. Understanding this concept explains why previous world models failed and why this result, if it holds, is foundational.
